body.en: The gradient of a curve from first principles, the power rule for differentiation, and reversing it to integrate.

\( \dfrac{d}{dx}x^{n}=nx^{n-1} \); the gradient at a point is the value of \( \tfrac{dy}{dx} \) there. Integration reverses this: \( \displaystyle\int x^{n}\,dx=\dfrac{x^{n+1}}{n+1}+C \) for \( n\neq-1 \).

Accumulation, Antiderivatives & Differential Flows: By the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, the accumulation function \(A(x) = \int_a^x f(t)\,dt\) satisfies \(A'(x) = f(x)\), linking instantaneous rates of change to net signed area. In first-order differential equations \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = g(x)h(y)\), separation of variables \(\int \dfrac{1}{h(y)}\,dy = \int g(x)\,dx + C\) reconstructs the family of integral curves across the slope field.

body.en:
Algebraic preparation: Express all algebraic fractions and surds in index form before differentiating or integrating: \(\frac{3}{x^2} = 3x^{-2}\), \(4\sqrt{x} = 4x^{1/2}\), \(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}} = \frac{1}{2}x^{-1/2}\). Differentiating denominators directly without rewriting produces invalid derivatives.

Tangent vs Normal: The tangent line has gradient \(m_{\text{tan}} = \frac{dy}{dx}\). The normal line is perpendicular, having gradient \(m_{\text{norm}} = -\frac{1}{m_{\text{tan}}}\). Both lines pass through the exact same point \((x_1, y_1)\) on the curve.

Area between curves: Area is \(\int_a^b (y_{\text{top}} - y_{\text{bottom}})\,dx\). If a curve crosses the \(x\)-axis within the limits of integration, integrating across the roots will result in positive and negative areas cancelling out. You must integrate each section separately and sum the positive areas.

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Differentiation & Integration)

body.en:
Why Integration by Parts & Integrating Factors Work: Differentiating a product \(u(x)v(x)\) gives \((uv)' = u'v + uv'\). Integrating both sides and rearranging yields the Integration by Parts formula:

\[ \int u\,\frac{dv}{dx}\,dx = u v - \int v\,\frac{du}{dx}\,dx \]

Similarly, for a linear first-order ODE \(y' + P(x)y = Q(x)\), multiplying by the integrating factor \(\mu(x) = e^{\int P(x)\,dx}\) (which satisfies \(\mu'(x) = P(x)\mu(x)\)) collapses the left-hand side into an exact product derivative: \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\bigl[\mu(x)y\bigr] = \mu(x)Q(x)\).

rows.en: Writing \(\ln|y| = x^2 + C \implies y = e^{x^2} + C\)
Exponentiation distributes over addition as multiplication (\(e^{a+b} = e^a e^b\)), not addition.
Write \(y = e^{x^2 + C} = Ae^{x^2}\) and solve for \(A\) using the initial condition.
Leaving original \(x\)-limits on a \(u\)-substituted definite integral
Evaluates the antiderivative \(F(u)\) at \(x\)-values instead of \(u(x)\)-values.
Convert bounds immediately: \(u_{\text{low}} = u(a)\) and \(u_{\text{high}} = u(b)\).
Cancels forward and backward motion (net displacement) instead of accumulating total path length.
Split the integral at every root where \(v(t) = 0\) and integrate \(|v(t)|\).

question.en: A curve has equation \(y = 2x^3 - 9x^2 + 12x + 1\). (a) Find the coordinates of both stationary points. (b) Determine the nature of each stationary point using the second derivative \(\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}\).

question.en: Find the exact area of the region enclosed between the curve \(y = 4x - x^2\) and the line \(y = x\).
question.ar: أوجد exact area of the region enclosed between the curve \(y = 4x - x^2\) and the line \(y = x\).

solution.en:
Find points of intersection: \[4x - x^2 = x \Rightarrow 3x - x^2 = 0 \Rightarrow x(3 - x) = 0\] The curves intersect at \(x = 0\) and \(x = 3\). Between \(0\) and \(3\), the curve \(y = 4x - x^2\) lies above the line \(y = x\).
The enclosed area is: \[A = \int_0^3 \left[(4x - x^2) - x\right]\,dx = \int_0^3 (3x - x^2)\,dx\] Integrate: \[A = \left[\dfrac{3x^2}{2} - \dfrac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^3 = \left(\dfrac{3(9)}{2} - \dfrac{27}{3}\right) - 0 = \dfrac{27}{2} - 9 = \dfrac{27 - 18}{2} = \dfrac{9}{2} = 4.5\]

question.en: Find the equation of the normal to the curve \(y = \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{x}} + 2x\) at the point where \(x = 4\).
question.ar: أوجد equation of the normal to the curve \(y = \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{x}} + 2x\) عند النقطة حيث \(x = 4\).

solution.en:
Rewrite in index form: \(y = 4x^{-1/2} + 2x\).
At \(x = 4\): \(y = 4(4^{-1/2}) + 2(4) = 4\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right) + 8 = 2 + 8 = 10\). Point of contact is \((4, 10)\).
Differentiate: \[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 4\left(-\tfrac{1}{2}x^{-3/2}\right) + 2 = -2x^{-3/2} + 2 = -\dfrac{2}{x^{3/2}} + 2\] At \(x = 4\): \(x^{3/2} = (\sqrt{4})^3 = 8\). Thus: \[m_{\text{tan}} = -\dfrac{2}{8} + 2 = -\dfrac{1}{4} + 2 = \dfrac{7}{4}\] The normal has gradient \(m_{\text{norm}} = -\dfrac{1}{7/4} = -\dfrac{4}{7}\).
Using point \((4, 10)\): \[y - 10 = -\dfrac{4}{7}(x - 4) \Rightarrow 7(y - 10) = -4(x - 4) \Rightarrow 7y - 70 = -4x + 16 \Rightarrow 4x + 7y - 86 = 0\]

question.en: [Practice 4 · Easy] The diagram shows part of the curve with equation \( y = x^2 - 4x + 5 \) and the point \( P(3, 2) \) lying on the curve. Find the gradient of the tangent to the curve at the point \( P \).
question.ar: [Practice 4 · Easy] The diagram shows part of the curve with equation \( y = x^2 - 4x + 5 \) and the point \( P(3, 2) \) lying on the curve. أوجد gradient of the tangent to the curve عند النقطة \( P \).

hints.en: To find the gradient of the tangent to the curve at \( P(3, 2) \), we determine the derivative \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} \) and evaluate it at \( x = 3 \).
hints.ar: To أوجد gradient of the tangent to the curve at \( P(3, 2) \), we حدّد derivative \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} \) and احسب قيمة it at \( x = 3 \).

hints.en: Differentiate \( y = x^2 - 4x + 5 \) with respect to \( x \) using the power rule: \(\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = 2x - 4\).
hints.ar: Dإذا كانferentiate \( y = x^2 - 4x + 5 \) بالنسبة إلى \( x \) باستخدام power rule: \(\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = 2x - 4\).

solution.en:
To find the gradient of the tangent to the curve at \( P(3, 2) \), we determine the derivative \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} \) and evaluate it at \( x = 3 \).

1. Differentiate \( y = x^2 - 4x + 5 \) with respect to \( x \) using the power rule:
\[ \frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = 2x - 4 \]

2. Substitute \( x = 3 \) into the derivative:
\[ \left.\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}\right|_{x=3} = 2(3) - 4 = 6 - 4 = 2 \]

Common errors:
- \( 6 \) occurs if only the first term is differentiated (giving \( 2x \)) and evaluated at \( x = 3 \), omitting the derivative of \( -4x \).
- \( -4 \) incorrectly takes the linear coefficient without differentiating the quadratic term.
- \( \dfrac{2}{3} \) confuses the instantaneous gradient of the tangent with the gradient of the line from the origin to \( P \), \( \dfrac{y}{x} = \dfrac{2}{3} \).
